data.name: Ciel Fledge: A Daughter Raising Simulator
data.detailed_description:
CRIA O FUTURO


No ano 3716, a humanidade vive sob risco constante de ruína perante uma colossal ameaça alienígena chamada “GIGANT”. Fugindo da destruição, uma misteriosa jovem chega a ARK-3, uma cidade magnífica construída no céu…

Ciel Fledge é um jogo sobre criar uma filha adotiva num mundo futuro que ainda tem esperança. Com uma gestão cativante e um elenco adorável de personagens, a tua tarefa é criar Ciel até ela atingir a idade adulta e estar preparada para abandonar o ninho.

Supervisiona - Monitoriza as atividades diárias e analisa o comportamento de Ciel. Fica de olho na disposição, pois Ciel poderá abandonar atividades se ficar demasiado cansada. Aumenta a resistência com itens, mima-a com uma mesada generosa ou repreende-a quando faltar à escola. Tu decides de que forma a vais criar.

Batalha - Os desafios da vida quotidiana assumem a forma de desafiadoras batalhas com puzzles: conclui uma atividade ou passa num teste ganhando jogos estratégicos de combinações de cartas. Aprende técnicas e cria amizades para ganhar apoio extra nas batalhas.

Cresce - Cada escolha afeta o crescimento de Ciel. Acompanha o progresso semanalmente e vê como mudaram as estatísticas e as relações dela – com centenas de características desbloqueáveis que podem afetar as interações e as capacidades de Ciel em batalha.

Personaliza - Cada Ciel é única. Há uma série de roupas e equipamentos, bem como múltiplos finais, pelo que a pessoa em que ela se torna depende de como a moldas. A idade, a altura e até o peso mudarão com o passar dos anos.

Explora - Envia Ciel em expedições à superfície da Terra para explorar e descobrir novas áreas do velho mundo. Vasculha itens úteis e une-te a amigos para combater inimigos e aumentar imenso as estatísticas.

Descontrai - Contempla as paisagens e os sons da cidade e adapta-te à rotina diária de ARK-3. Inclui uma arte encantadora e uma banda sonora instrumental inspirada na pop urbana japonesa.

reviews.review:
Ciel Fledge: A Daughter Raising Simulator approaches the life simulation genre from an uncommon direction, placing the responsibilities of parenthood inside a distant science-fiction future. Developed by Studio Namaapa and published by PQube, the game puts you in charge of raising an adopted girl named Ciel from childhood until adulthood. Rather than controlling every aspect of her life directly, you shape her future through schedules, education, hobbies, friendships, employment, equipment, and countless smaller decisions. The result is a management-focused experience where long-term consequences matter considerably more than immediate victories.

The setting gives the otherwise familiar raising-simulator formula an intriguing backdrop. Humanity has abandoned Earth after suffering devastation caused by a colossal alien threat known as GIGANT. By the year 3716, survivors live in enormous settlements constructed above the ruined planet, including the airborne city of ARK-3. Ciel arrives under mysterious circumstances and is placed in your care. Despite this grim premise, the game generally maintains a hopeful and comfortable atmosphere. Daily routines, family responsibilities, school life, friendships, and personal growth receive considerably more attention than apocalyptic destruction, creating an effective contrast between an endangered civilization and the ordinary experience of watching a child grow up.

Most of the gameplay revolves around planning Ciel's schedule. Each week presents opportunities to assign classes, hobbies, jobs, social activities, and other tasks. These activities influence different statistics and gradually determine the type of person she becomes. There is considerable temptation to maximize every available day, but constantly keeping Ciel busy is not necessarily beneficial. Fatigue must be considered alongside development, and excessive scheduling can cause problems with her behavior and performance. This creates a surprisingly meaningful balancing act. You are not simply maximizing statistics but deciding when Ciel should work, learn, socialize, explore, or recover.

Her physical and personal development reinforces the feeling that time is genuinely passing. Ciel grows older as the years advance, with characteristics such as her height and weight changing alongside her abilities and personality. Outfits and equipment provide further customization, while friendships and activities can affect her development in different ways. The numerous possible traits and outcomes encourage experimentation because one playthrough cannot easily represent every possible version of her life. Different priorities can eventually produce different endings, making replaying the game particularly appealing for players who enjoy exploring alternative development paths.

Ciel Fledge also introduces more active mechanics instead of functioning entirely through menus. Various challenges are represented through puzzle-oriented battles, including match-three style mechanics that transform everyday activities into more interactive encounters. Friends and learned techniques can provide useful advantages. These systems give the player something more immediate to control between periods of scheduling and management. They are inventive, although they can also become repetitive after many hours. Players primarily interested in the parenting simulation may occasionally feel that these sequences interrupt the management flow rather than strengthen it.

Exploration provides another welcome change of pace. Ciel can travel on expeditions to Earth's surface, discover locations, gather useful resources, confront enemies, and cooperate with companions. These journeys connect the relatively peaceful existence aboard ARK-3 with the larger science-fiction story. They also provide opportunities for substantial character development and statistical improvement. While exploration is not deep enough to turn the game into a traditional adventure RPG, it gives the world additional scale and prevents Ciel's entire existence from feeling restricted to menus and weekly schedules.

Presentation is one of the game's more charming qualities. Its colorful anime-inspired artwork fits the optimistic tone, while ARK-3 creates a pleasant environment despite humanity's difficult circumstances. The soundtrack is particularly memorable, using smooth instrumental music influenced by Japanese City Pop. It complements the repetitive but relaxing routine of organizing schedules, monitoring Ciel's development, and preparing for another week. Combined with the character designs, the music helps establish a warmer personality than the game's post-apocalyptic background initially suggests.

The main weakness is repetition. Raising Ciel takes place across a long period, and the basic rhythm of scheduling activities, watching results, managing resources, and repeating the process inevitably becomes familiar. Players who love statistical optimization may find this addictive, while those expecting constant narrative developments could lose interest. Some mechanics also require patience before their long-term value becomes obvious. The experience is therefore best approached as a slow management simulation rather than a conventional story-driven RPG.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially listed as Unknown rather than Verified, Playable, or Unsupported. The PC version does support Linux and offers full controller support, which are encouraging characteristics for portable play, but the absence of an official Steam Deck compatibility rating means players should not interpret those features as a guarantee of a completely trouble-free Deck experience.

Ultimately, Ciel Fledge succeeds because its many statistics and management systems serve a simple emotional idea: watching someone grow according to the opportunities and guidance you provide. The individual mechanics are not always equally polished, and repetition keeps the experience from reaching its full potential, but the combination of parenting simulation, scheduling, relationships, puzzle encounters, exploration, multiple endings, and science-fiction world-building is genuinely distinctive. Players who enjoy patient character management and seeing long-term decisions gradually produce consequences will find the experience especially rewarding.

Rating: 7/10
